title: Ethical Data Acquisition Audit
audience: Basic science learners auditing whether biomedical datasets are ethically acquired and fit for AI use.
objectives: Review autonomy, justice, privacy, and beneficence as data acquisition pillars.
Revise consent language for clearer participant understanding.
Evaluate representation gaps and recruitment strategies.
Select security controls and return-of-value practices.

sections.name: Intro: The Four Pillars
sections.purpose: Frame the ethical audit target and learner role.

sections.name: Autonomy: Consent Audit
sections.purpose: Compare legalistic consent language with participant-centered language.

sections.name: Justice: Representation Audit
sections.purpose: Use recruitment strategies to close representation gaps.

sections.name: Privacy: Security Audit
sections.purpose: Select layered security controls and inspect risk status.

sections.name: Beneficence: Impact Audit
sections.purpose: Complete the ethical data cycle by returning value to participants.

chatbot_guidance: Guide learners through the audit activity selector.
Explain the four pillars in practical biomedical data terms.
Help interpret pass or fail states without overcomplicating the answer.
